problemStatement.formal: For any polynomial p and n×n matrix A over a commutative ring R: aeval A p = aeval A (p %ₘ A.charpoly), where the remainder has degree < n.
problemStatement.plain: Any polynomial function of a matrix A can be reduced modulo its characteristic polynomial. This means p(A) depends only on the remainder of p divided by charpoly(A), reducing matrix computations to polynomials of degree < n.
whyMatters: Enables efficient computation of matrix powers A^k via polynomial arithmetic
Provides algebraic foundation for computing matrix exponentials exp(tA)
Shows evaluation map factors through finite-dimensional quotient ring R[X]/(charpoly)

proven: aeval_eq_aeval_modByMonic: aeval A p = aeval A (p mod charpoly(A))
degree_reduced_lt_dim: Reduced polynomial has degree < n
power_eq_aeval_mod: A^k = aeval A (X^k mod charpoly(A))
congruence: Same remainder mod charpoly implies same matrix evaluation
charpoly_multiple_annihilates: Multiples of charpoly annihilate A
annihilator_add: Annihilator is closed under addition
annihilator_mul_left: Annihilator is closed under left multiplication
partial_sum_reduces: Finite power series reduce via charpoly
idempotent_power: A^2 = A implies A^k = A for all k > 0
knownResults.goal: Prove the polynomial reduction theorem and its consequences for matrix functions

insights: The polynomial division algorithm for monic polynomials is the key tool - charpoly is always monic
Cayley-Hamilton (aeval A charpoly(A) = 0) makes the quotient term vanish
The evaluation map R[X] -> M_n(R) factors through R[X]/(charpoly), dimension n as R-module
For nilpotent matrices, the exponential series truncates exactly after n terms
For idempotent matrices, exp(tA) = I + (e^t - 1)*A - a one-coefficient formula

approaches.name: Polynomial division modulo monic charpoly
